newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Profit-taking continues on Budapest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking continues on Budapest bourse.

text.p: Hungarian share prices declined on Friday as profit-taking continued to take its toll on the market which apparently received only little help from the dollar's strength, traders said.
"Thursday's trend continued as there was some profit-taking," said Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings.
The BUX index closed at 5,657.33 points, down 100.49.
BUX futures fell 81.50 points to 6,150 for March but rose for the five other maturities by 9.50 to 96.00 points.
On the spot market stock prices headed downwards in early trading but the trend reversed and the papers closed above their daily lows.

"Share prices edged a little higher after they reached their bottom within the first third of trading time was over," Czipo said. "The market overreacted the downward trend so prices rebounded slightly from the bottom."
Oil and gas company MOL shares led the market's downward trend in an enourmous volume of nearly 670,000 stocks.
MOL opened sharply lower, at 3,300 forints compared to Thursday's close of 3,500, and tumbled to a daily low of 3,200 forints from where it rebounded to close at 3,300.
Traders said many big investors regarded MOL's recent price attractive to sell and speculators joined the trend.
"Investors reacted naturally after such a huge rise in MOL prices recently," Czipo said.
Elsewhere on the market beverage stocks closed lower with the exception of brewery Martfu which remained steady at 3,000.
Spirits maker Zwack dropped 3.51 percent to 5,500, brewery Sopron fell 2.97 percent to 4,900 while mineral water bottler and distributor Kekkuti lost 2.96 percent and closed at 1,310.
Pharmaceuticals stocks ended mixed, chemicals and banks were slightly weaker, meat food processor Pick and hotelier Danubius moved higher.
